assign.title: You are a mastermind on Sonnet, medium effort; budget about $5. Two Recite fixes from the owner (via voice, 16:45). Work

log.text: Built in worktree recite-cue (commit on worktree/recite-cue): cue now only on {thinking:{by:smart}} line, repeats until reply; resume icon ink fixed to #1a1008 on orange (~9:1). Headless check on worktree site: plain line 0 cues, thinking line plays+repeats, stops on reply. Review running, then merge.

findings.text: The repeating cue has no end except a reply that has text: `start_thinking()` reschedules itself while `cue_pending` is true (Recite.js, `start_thinking`), and `partial("")` (the end of the stream) never calls `cancel_cue()` (Recite.js:320 cancels only `if (text)`). If the agent fires `thinking` and then sends an empty reply (session-smart.md:58 tells it to stay silent sometimes) or its turn fails, the phone beeps every 2 s until the owner speaks again. The owner already finds the cue annoying. Fix: cap the repeats (for example 30 s), or cancel on the stream's end too.

The brief is missing from the task folder: there is no `requirements.md`, so a fresh agent (or this reviewer) can't see the two asks without digging through the agent's transcript. Save the spawn prompt as `requirements.md` beside `session.jsonl`.

The brief asked for two merges, with the cue fix "FIRST, as its own small merge". Both fixes are in one commit, da0d972af, on `worktree/recite-cue`, which is not merged into michael/dev yet. Either split it, or record why one merge was chosen.

The brief asked for a shot of the resume button at 360x740 (ask 2). There is none in the task folder (no `shots/`). The contrast claim ("about 9:1", Recite.css:35) is not checked anywhere, and the brief also asked for a 2-line report to vscode-mastermind and a closed task. `session.jsonl` has no landing line.

Old comments still describe the automatic cue. Recite.test.mjs:377-379 still says "a short tone once the owner's line lands, again cue_repeat_ms later... then quiet". Recite.js:50 (`cue_timer`) still says "expect_reply()'s own pending timeout for the second cue". doc/architecture.md:32 ("Why any non-assistant chat.text is close enough… chime once a line was sent") still argues for the trigger that was just removed. Update or delete each one.

Recite.css:35 hard-codes `#1a1008`. framework.css:605 already sets the ink on orange for `.bg-prime` as `#1a1a1a`. Reusing that value (or that class) keeps one ink-on-prime colour instead of two. The comment should also go on its own line; at 170 characters it runs past the declaration it explains.

Ask 1 is met as described: a plain line now only sets `cue_pending` (`expect_reply`), the `{thinking:{by:"smart"}}` line plays the cue and repeats it, `thinking_cue` is kept, and the readme and session-smart.md each say in one line how to fire it. The 120 s staleness guard in `from_wire` covers only `chat.at`. A `thinking` line has no timestamp check, so if the wire ever replays old lines, a stale one would start the cue. Today `Session.stream` sends live lines only (ext/Session/Session.js:158), so this is a watch-out, not a bug.
`Recite/ai/files.jsonl` gains one more `log.jsonl` "gone" line; that line is noise from the machine log and is unrelated to either ask.
